recommendedTextbook.title: New General Mathematics for Senior Secondary Schools 1
recommendedTextbook.author: M.F. Macrae, A.O. Kalejaiye, Z.I. Chima, G.U. Garba

topics.topic: Number Bases: Operations and Equations in Various Bases
subtopics: Review of Base 2, 8, 10, and 16 conversions
Addition, subtraction, and multiplication in bases other than 10
Solving equations involving unknown number bases: e.g., 23_x + 101_2 = 35_10
objectives: Perform arithmetic operations in arbitrary number bases (Base 2 through Base 12)
Set up and solve algebraic equations to determine unknown base values (x)
Relate octal and hexadecimal bases to microcomputer architecture

topics.topic: Modular Arithmetic: Operations in Finite Clocks & Residue Classes
subtopics: Concept of modular systems (clock arithmetic: Modulo 12, Modulo 7 for days of week)
Addition, subtraction, and multiplication tables in modulo arithmetic
Solving modular linear equations in Nigerian calendar and market day cycles
objectives: Define modulo arithmetic and calculate residues
Construct operational tables for modulo arithmetic systems
Apply modulo 4 and modulo 7 to traditional Nigerian market rotations (Eke, Oye, Afor, Nkwo)

topics.topic: Indices: Laws of Indices, Fractional & Negative Powers
subtopics: Statutory laws of indices: multiplication, division, power of power, zero index
Negative indices (a^-n = 1/a^n) and fractional indices (a^(m/n) = n-th root of a^m)
Solving exponential equations where the unknown is an index
objectives: Apply all laws of indices to simplify complex algebraic fractions
Solve exponential equations of the form 2^(2x+1) - 9(2^x) + 4 = 0

topics.topic: Logarithms: Properties and Computations Using Four-Figure Tables
subtopics: Relationship between indices and logarithms: log_b(a) = c <=> b^c = a
Laws of logarithms (addition, subtraction, power, and change of base)
Using four-figure logarithm tables for calculations of products, quotients, roots, and powers
objectives: State and apply properties of logarithms to simplify expressions
Perform complex scientific multiplications and cube roots using logarithm tables

topics.topic: Sets: Set Operations, Venn Diagrams and 2-Set Problems
subtopics: Definition of set, elements, subsets, universal set, empty set, complement of a set
Union (∪) and Intersection (∩) operations and Venn diagram representations
Solving 2-set surveying word problems: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B)
objectives: Draw and shade regions on Venn diagrams representing set operations
Solve 2-set survey word problems from Nigerian school and market scenarios

topics.topic: Simple Equations and Variations: Direct, Inverse, Joint and Partial
subtopics: Formulating algebraic equations from practical verbal statements
Solving simultaneous linear equations in two variables
Partial variation where one quantity is partly constant and partly varies with another: y = a + bx
objectives: Solve partial variation word problems determining the constants a and b
Apply partial variation to transport taxi tariffs and electric billing in Nigeria

subtopics: Diagnostic evaluation on bases, modulos, indices, logarithms, sets, and variation
WASSCE standard problem clinic
objectives: Assess pupil performance against WAEC marking guidelines

topics.topic: Quadratic Equations: Solution by Factorization & Completing the Square
subtopics: Review of factorization methods for quadratic equations
Method of completing the square step-by-step: making the leading coefficient 1
Derivation of the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b^2 - 4ac)] / 2a
objectives: Solve quadratic equations using completing the square method
Derive the general quadratic formula algebraically from ax^2 + bx + c = 0

topics.topic: Quadratic Formula and the Nature of Roots (Discriminant Δ)
subtopics: Using quadratic formula for decimal and non-factorizable quadratic equations
The discriminant: Δ = b^2 - 4ac
Conditions for real, distinct, equal, and complex/imaginary roots
objectives: Calculate roots to 2 decimal places using the quadratic formula
Determine the nature of roots without solving the equation using the discriminant

topics.topic: Logical Reasoning: Statements, Negation, Conjunction, Disjunction & Implications
subtopics: Propositions and truth values (True / False)
Logical operators: Negation (~p), Conjunction (p ∧ q), Disjunction (p ∨ q)
Conditional (p -> q) and bi-conditional (p <-> q) statements and truth tables
objectives: Identify valid logical statements and determine their truth values
Construct complete truth tables for compound logical propositions
Distinguish between converse, inverse, and contrapositive statements

topics.topic: Mensuration: Length of Arc, Perimeter of Sector, Area of Sector & Segment
subtopics: Length of an arc: L = (θ / 360°) × 2πr
Area of a sector of a circle: A = (θ / 360°) × πr^2
Perimeter of a sector (2r + L) and Area of segment = Area of sector - Area of triangle
objectives: Calculate arc lengths, sector perimeters, and sector areas in degrees and radians
Find the area of shaded segments in circular engineering designs

topics.topic: Comprehensive Termly Revision & WASSCE Past Question Clinic
subtopics: Review of senior algebra, logarithms, quadratic equations, and circular mensuration
Timed 50-question WAEC Objective & Theory drill
objectives: Solve WASSCE past questions with proper M-marks and A-marks workings

subtopics: First Term Senior Examination and continuous assessment moderation
objectives: Complete SSS 1 General Mathematics Term 1 evaluation
